facts.text: I am using Stable Diffusion txt2img to generate images from prompts.
I am using a fine-tuning model that is biased to produce attractive women.
I manually adjusted a prompt for 'the fool' to something closer to what I would expect to give good results from the image generator.
The prompt I adjusted includes 'digital illustration for The Fool Tarot card'.
The prompt I adjusted includes 'a carefree young man running near the edge of a cliff'.
The prompt I adjusted includes multiple artist/style references: Pamela Colman Smith, Salvador Dali, Alex Grey, Brian Froud, and Yoshitaka Amano.
The prompt I adjusted includes 'intricate silver border of intertwining vines and celestial motifs'.
I believe proper grammar is not necessary for my prompts because every word impacts the output.
I believe early words in the prompt are given more weight by the model.
I believe too long a prompt may yield diminishing returns.
I believe too short a prompt may yield erratic outputs with less consistency.
I believe too short a prompt may too strongly emulate a particular piece of training data.
I have observed that gender neutral nouns like 'youth', 'figure', and 'person' tend to generate only women.
I have observed that the generated women are often in an undesirably sensual style.
For ambiguous characters such as 'the fool', I want the traditional gender selected or the gender specified.
If it would be unusual for the character to be depicted in a sensual style and the character is a woman, I want a description of her attire included.
Alternatively, I can make the design choice to lean into sensual styles and make all characters female.

keyphrases: intricate silver border vines celestial motifs
